passage.title: Mystery of Elephant Communication
paragraphs: A. O'Connel-Rodwell, a postdoctoral fellow from Stanford University, came to Namibia's foremost wildlife sanctuary, Etosha, to find out more about the little-known subject of elephant communication. Almost 20 years ago, researchers, including O'Connel-Rodwell made the surprising discovery that elephants communicate over long distances using extremely low-frequency sounds, also called infrasound, which are generally too deep to be heard by humans.

B. It is possible to find some clues to the elephant's ability to hear infrasound within the structure of the ear itself. The hammer bone of the elephant's inner ear is proportionally very large, which is typical for other animals that use vibrational signals. Additionally, the elephant and its relative, the manatees, are unusual among mammals for having a cochlear structure in the inner ear which is similar to that of many reptiles. In reptiles, this cochlear structure facilitates keen sensitivity to vibrations, and the same seems to be indicated in elephants.

C. There are other indications in the elephant's anatomy to support their ability to hear infrasound. Firstly, the sheer size of their bodies allows them to generate low-frequency sounds which can be almost as powerful as a jet take-off. Their large bodies also provide ideal 'frames' for receiving vibrations through the ground and up to their heads. Secondly, their toe bones rest on fatty pads which may help to focus vibrations from the ground into the bone. Thirdly, the way the elephant brain lies within the cranial cavity, behind the eyes and in line with the auditory canal, may help them feel the vibrations. The front of the skull has many sinus cavities which might function as resonating chambers for receiving the vibrations from the ground.

D. O'Connel-Rodwell’s background reveals the reason why she was the one to realize that elephants used seismic communication. “I did my master's thesis on seismic communication in planthoppers, ”she wrote. “I'd put a male planthopper on a stem and play back a female call, and the male would do the same thing the elephants were doing：He would freeze, then press down on his legs, go forward a little bit, then freeze again. It was just so fascinating to me, and it's what got me to think, maybe there's something else going on other than acoustic communication.”It was already known that seismic communication is common in a number of small animals such as spiders, scorpions, frogs, blind mole rats, kangaroo rats, elephant seals and golden moles, but O'Connell-Rodwell was the first to realize that such a large mammal could also use the method.

E. Further research has shown that this ability to communicate over long distances is actually essential to the survival of the species. For example, if a predator is detected in the area, experienced members of the herd emit intense warning calls which prompt the herd members to come together for safety and then leave the area. In 1994, O'Connell-Rodwell recorded the warning sounds of a breeding herd being threatened by lions at Mushara. “The elephants got really scared, and the matriarch, the oldest and largest female cow, made these very powerful warning calls, and then the herd took off screaming and trumpeting, ”she recalls, “Since then，every time we played that particular call at the water hole, we get the same response-the elephants take off."

F. In this case, the warning sounds are transmitted through the air, so researchers wanted to find out more about whether elephants could detect calls transmitted through the ground. In 2002，they devised an experiment using electronic equipment that allowed them to send signals through the ground. “The results of our 2002 study showed us that elephants do indeed detect warning calls played through the ground, ”O'Connell-Rodwell observed. “We expected them to clump up into tight groups and leave the areas, and that's in fact what they did. But since we only played back one type of call, we coudn't really say whether they were interpreting it correctly.” Clearly, further study was needed as the elephants may interpret the sound as something strange.

G. Another experiment in the same area in 2004 was aimed at further studying elephants' sound-detecting abilities by using three different recordings-the 1994 warning call from Mushara, an anti-predator call recorded by scientist Joyce Poole in Kenya, and an artificial warble tone. The recordings were played at random and at various times to see if the elephants would recognize them as distinct vibrations. O'Connel-Rodwell explained that the aim was to determine whether they can discriminate between familiar and unfamiliar calls that are played back as seismic signals. Even though the analysis phase of the research data from the 2004 experiment is still under way, O'Connell-Rodwell is able to make a few preliminary observations and conclude that the reactions of the elephants were exactly as expected. “When the 1994 warning call was played back, they tended to clump together and leave the water hole sooner. But what's really interesting is that the unfamiliar anti-predator call from Kenya also caused them to clump up, get nervous and aggressively rumble, but they didn't necessarily leave. I didn't think it was going to be that clear-cut.

questions.text: O'Connell-Rodwell chose a less known method to research about the ways elephants communicate.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
O'Connell-Rodwell đã chọn một phương pháp ít được biết đến để nghiên cứu về cách mà voi giao tiếp.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
little-known subject of elephant communication ~ less known method
O'Connel-Rodwell ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
communication ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "O'Connel-Rodwell, một nghiên cứu sinh tiến sĩ từ Đại học Stanford, đã đến khu bảo tồn động vật hoang dã hàng đầu của Namibia, Etosha, để tìm hiểu thêm về chủ đề ít được biết đến về giao tiếp của voi".
=> Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không hề nhắc đến thông tin "O'Connell-Rodwell đã chọn một phương pháp ít được biết đến" (chose a less known method). Bài chỉ nói rằng "chủ đề giao tiếp của voi" là ít được biết đến, nhưng không đề cập đến việc cô ấy chọn một phương pháp ít được biết đến.
Bước 4: Đáp án: NOT GIVEN
quotes: A. O'Connel-Rodwell, a postdoctoral fellow from Stanford University, came to Namibia's foremost wildlife sanctuary, Etosha, to find out more about the little-known subject of elephant communication.

questions.text: The elephant's body acts as a good transmitter of vibration signals.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Cơ thể của voi hoạt động như một máy phát tín hiệu rung động tốt.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
large bodies ~ elephant's body
size of their bodies allows them to generate low-frequency sounds ~ acts as a good transmitter
vibrations ~ vibration signals

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Thứ nhất, kích thước cơ thể to lớn cho phép chúng tạo ra âm thanh tần số thấp có thể mạnh gần bằng tiếng máy bay cất cánh. Cơ thể lớn của chúng cũng cung cấp 'khung' lý tưởng để nhận các rung động qua mặt đất và lên đến đầu của chúng".
=> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Cơ thể của voi hoạt động như một máy phát tín hiệu rung động tốt" (The elephant's body acts as a good transmitter of vibration signals).
Bước 4: Đáp án: TRUE
quotes: Firstly, the sheer size of their bodies allows them to generate low-frequency sounds which can be almost as powerful as a jet take-off. Their large bodies also provide ideal 'frames' for receiving vibrations through the ground and up to their heads.

questions.text: O’Connel-Rodwell's research indicates that only small animals have potential in seismic communication.
quotes: ”It was already known that seismic communication is common in a number of small animals such as spiders, scorpions, frogs, blind mole rats, kangaroo rats, elephant seals and golden moles, but O'Connell-Rodwell was the first to realize that such a large mammal could also use the method.

questions.text: In the 1994 experiment, it was found that all the old elephants sent out danger signals and left with other elephants.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Trong thí nghiệm năm 1994, người ta phát hiện ra rằng tất cả những con voi già đều phát ra tín hiệu nguy hiểm và rời đi cùng với những con voi khác.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
1994 ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
matriarch, the oldest and largest female cow, made these very powerful warning calls ~ all the old elephants sent out danger signals
the herd took off ~ left with other elephants

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc đề cập đến việc "Năm 1994, O'Connell-Rodwell đã ghi lại âm thanh cảnh báo của một đàn voi sinh sản đang bị sư tử đe dọa tại Mushara. "Những con voi thực sự sợ hãi, và con voi cái đầu đàn, con voi cái lớn tuổi và to lớn nhất, đã phát ra những tiếng kêu cảnh báo rất mạnh, và sau đó đàn voi bỏ chạy, hét và kêu trumpet,"".
=> Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không hề nhắc đến thông tin "tất cả những con voi già đều phát ra tín hiệu nguy hiểm" (all the old elephants sent out danger signals). Bài chỉ nói về một con voi cái đầu đàn.

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE
quotes: “The elephants got really scared, and the matriarch, the oldest and largest female cow, made these very powerful warning calls, and then the herd took off screaming and trumpeting, ”she recalls, “Since then，every time we played that particular call at the water hole, we get the same response-the elephants take off.

questions.text: The results of 2002 study partially proved the relation between warning calls and elephants' reaction.
quotes: “The results of our 2002 study showed us that elephants do indeed detect warning calls played through the ground, ”O'Connell-Rodwell observed. “We expected them to clump up into tight groups and leave the areas, and that's in fact what they did. But since we only played back one type of call, we coudn't really say whether they were interpreting it correctly.” Clearly, further study was needed as the elephants may interpret the sound as something strange.

questions.text: Joyce Poole played a key role in investigating elephants' sound-detecting abilities.
quotes: G. Another experiment in the same area in 2004 was aimed at further studying elephants' sound-detecting abilities by using three different recordings-the 1994 warning call from Mushara, an anti-predator call recorded by scientist Joyce Poole in Kenya, and an artificial warble tone.

Thí nghiệm năm 2004 đã làm rõ rằng

Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Khi tiếng kêu cảnh báo năm 1994 được phát lại, chúng có xu hướng tụ tập lại và rời khỏi hố nước sớm hơn. Nhưng điều thực sự thú vị là tiếng kêu chống kẻ săn mồi không quen thuộc từ Kenya cũng khiến chúng tụ tập lại, trở nên lo lắng và gầm gừ hung hăng, nhưng chúng không nhất thiết phải bỏ đi. Tôi đã không nghĩ rằng nó sẽ rõ ràng như vậy."
=> Thông tin được in đậm đồng nghĩa với câu D (voi biết sự khác biệt giữa âm thanh quen thuộc và không quen thuộc).
